hints: Count the carbons carefully, you start with a 3-carbon bromoalkane but need to finish with a 4-carbon acid.
Remember which nucleophile can replace Br and add one extra carbon at the same time.
Think about what functional group hydrolyses in hot acid to give a carboxylic acid in the second step.
walkthrough:
**Count carbons to spot the problem**

Great start is to compare the skeletons. 1-bromopropane has 3 carbons, but butanoic acid has 4 carbons.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \; (3C) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \; (4C)$$
So the first step must add one carbon.

**Use cyanide to extend the chain**

The classic way to add one carbon is nucleophilic substitution with cyanide ion, $\text{CN}^-$. It replaces Br with $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N} + \text{Br}^-$$
The product is butanenitrile, with the nitrile carbon as the new fourth carbon. Conditions are ethanolic $\text{KCN}$ with heat.

**Hydrolyse the nitrile to the acid**

In the second step, the nitrile is hydrolysed by refluxing with dilute hydrochloric acid to give the carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
That confirms butanenitrile must be made first.

options.A: 1-aminopropane is made by reacting 1-bromopropane with excess ethanolic ammonia. It still has only 3 carbons and an amine group cannot be hydrolysed to a carboxylic acid, so it is a dead end for this synthesis.
options.B: Propan-1-ol is made by reacting 1-bromopropane with aqueous NaOH. It still has only 3 carbons, and its oxidation would give propanoic acid, not butanoic acid, so it does not solve the chain length problem.
options.C: Butanal does oxidise to butanoic acid, so it looks tempting. However butanal already has 4 carbons and cannot be made directly from 1-bromopropane in one substitution step, so it cannot be the first intermediate.
options.D: Butanenitrile is correct. Reaction with ethanolic KCN replaces Br by CN and adds the needed fourth carbon. Subsequent acid hydrolysis of the nitrile gives butanoic acid, completing the two-step sequence.
